Hello, world — and everything in between

meta personal

Hello, world — and everything in between

Starting a blog feels a lot like pushing code for the first time. You know that what you're about to share is imperfect. You know there are things you haven't thought of. And yet — you commit and push anyway, because waiting for perfect means never shipping at all.

So, here I am. Shipping.

Why I'm doing this

I've been a developer for a while now. During that time, I've learned so many things from people who wrote them down — blog posts at 2am, threads that unlocked a concept I'd been stuck on for days, documentation written by someone who cared enough to explain the why, not just the how.

This blog is my attempt to give some of that back.

What you'll find here

A few things I think about a lot:

  • Front-end development — CSS architecture, accessibility, performance, the small joys and frustrations of building for the browser
  • Design — I'm learning. Slowly. But I love the language of design: hierarchy, rhythm, whitespace, how a 2px border can change everything
  • Open knowledge — why I believe information should be free, how open source changed my life, and the ethics of who gets to build the web
  • Activism at the intersection — technology isn't neutral. I want to talk about what it means to build with intention

A note on perfectionism

I'm a perfectionist recovering in public. Posts here might be short. They might be rough. They might change as I learn more.

That's fine. That's the point.

"Done is better than perfect" is the most annoying advice, right up until the moment it saves you.

Welcome. I'm glad you're here.
